request: 你说国际运营市场不等于全是直营。那加盟店卖得好，麦当劳自己到底赚的是哪部分钱？

requirements.text: 解释加盟店销售如何转化为麦当劳自身的租金、特许权使用费等收入，区分传统加盟与发展许可或附属公司模式、加盟店销售额与公司确认收入，并结合已有季度披露说明加盟餐厅利润口径及其不等于集团净利润。

summary: 加盟店销售通过合同约定的租金、特许权使用费等转化为麦当劳收入，并非全额并入公司收入，也非按加盟商净利润分成。传统加盟与发展许可模式的资本责任不同；加盟餐厅利润还需与集团净利润区分。

claims.text: 简单说：加盟店卖得好，麦当劳主要赚的是合同约定的租金、特许权使用费等，而不是把加盟店全部营业额记成自己的收入。相关收费主要与销售额挂钩，也不是按加盟商净利润分成。因此，加盟店销售改善通常有利于麦当劳相关收入，但不能把门店多卖的钱全部算成麦当劳多赚的钱。

constraints.basis: 合同机制及其方向性解释

critic_verdict.basis: 10-Q收入说明将加盟收入界定为租金、按销售额计算的特许权使用费及初始费用，而非加盟店全部销售额；传统加盟段也明确收费以销售额而非加盟商净利润为基础。销售改善通常有利于相关收入是合同机制的方向性解释，草稿未将其表述为固定比例的利润增长。

claims.text: 传统加盟模式下，麦当劳通常拥有餐厅土地和建筑，或取得长期租赁权；加盟商承担设备、招牌、座椅及装修等投入。麦当劳主要收取按销售额计算的租金和特许权使用费，其中租金设有最低支付额，并在新店开业或授予新加盟权时收取初始费用。具体费用因场地、公司投入及当地经营条件而异，不能套用一个统一收费比例。

critic_verdict.basis: 传统加盟段明确公司通常拥有或长期租赁土地及建筑，加盟商支付设备、招牌、座椅和装修投入；后续原文列明按销售额收取租金及特许权使用费、最低租金和初始费用。费用因场地、公司投入及当地条件而异，支持不能套用统一收费比例的提醒。

claims.text: 发展许可或附属公司模式下，经营方负责经营管理、提供资本（包括房地产权益），并开发和开设新餐厅；麦当劳通常不投入餐厅资本，主要收取按销售额计算的特许权使用费，通常还会在新店开业或授予新许可时收取初始费用。与传统加盟相比，这一模式的餐厅资本责任更多由经营方承担。

critic_verdict.basis: Developmental License or Affiliate标题下原文明确经营方负责管理、资本投入（包括房地产权益）及新店开发，公司通常不投入餐厅资本，收取按销售额计算的特许权使用费及通常的初始费用。草稿保留了“通常”的限定，并正确区分两类模式的资本责任。

claims.text: 落到2026年第三季度，公司收入表直接披露的加盟收入为44.87亿美元。这是麦当劳确认的加盟收入，不是加盟餐厅向顾客销售食品的全部营业额。

constraints.basis: 季度收入表原文直接披露，非计算结果

critic_verdict.basis: 收入表的Quarters Ended September 30、2026列下，Franchised revenues合计为4,487百万美元，换算为44.87亿美元正确，未误用上年或累计期间。收入定义说明该金额为公司收取的加盟费用，而非加盟餐厅全部营业额；这里只进行了单位换算。

display_check.label: 核验方式为原文审读，数字与期间、指标的对应关系需结合引文判断。

claims.text: 这些加盟收入还不是利润。公司将“加盟餐厅利润”（Franchised restaurant margins）定义为加盟收入减去加盟餐厅物业占用成本；这些成本包括租赁费用和折旧，因为麦当劳通常拥有或长期租赁相关土地及建筑。

constraints.basis: 公司披露的餐厅利润定义

critic_verdict.basis: Restaurant Margins原文明确将加盟餐厅利润定义为加盟收入减加盟餐厅物业占用成本，并说明成本包括租赁费用和折旧，原因是公司通常拥有或长期租赁餐厅土地及建筑。草稿准确区分收入与该层面的利润。

claims.text: 2026年第三季度，公司餐厅利润表直接披露的加盟餐厅利润为38.00亿美元。它只是扣除上述物业占用成本后的餐厅层面指标，并不等于再扣除集团管理费用、利息、税项等之后的集团净利润。

constraints.basis: 季度餐厅利润表原文直接披露；与集团净利润的会计口径区分

critic_verdict.basis: 季度餐厅利润表的2026年Franchised合计为3,800百万美元，即38.00亿美元；同段定义显示它仅扣除加盟物业占用成本，并非集团净利润。公告另列本季集团净利润2,486百万美元，也印证两者指标不同。草稿是在解释尚未涵盖集团管理费用、利息及税项等的口径差异，并未声称从加盟餐厅利润仅靠这些扣项即可完整调节至集团净利润。

display_check.label: 核验方式为原文审读，数字与期间、指标的对应关系需结合引文判断。

claims.text: 所以，“国际运营市场”说的是业务分部，而不是全部直营的所有权模式：2026年第三季度的餐厅利润表，在该分部下同时列有加盟餐厅利润和公司自营餐厅利润。看这个分部的表现时，需要区分麦当劳从加盟店收取的费用，与自营店销售扣除餐厅经营成本后留下的利润。

constraints.basis: 季度餐厅利润表及其指标定义

critic_verdict.basis: 2026年第三季度餐厅利润表在International Operated Markets下分别列有加盟餐厅利润1,645百万美元及自营餐厅利润299百万美元，支持该分部并非全部直营。表前定义还区分加盟费用扣物业成本与自营销售扣餐厅经营成本的口径，支持草稿的经营模式解释。

McDONALD'S REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS
•Global Systemwide sales* increased 4% to over $38 billion for the quarter
•Consolidated operating income increased 7% and adjusted operating income increased 8% for the quarter
•Systemwide sales to loyalty members across 70 loyalty markets were $41 billion for the trailing twelve-month period and more than $11 billion for the quarter
CHICAGO, IL - McDonald's Corporation today announced results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.
“McDonald’s delivered another quarter of global growth, with solid performance across much of our international business. In the U.S., we're encouraged by improvement as the quarter progressed following our intervention on value,” said Chris Kempczinski, Chairman and CEO. “We’re focused on building from here, strengthening the business today and investing in the next chapter of growth.”
Third quarter financial performance:
•Global comparable sales increased 1.5%:
•U.S. decreased 0.2%
•International Operated Markets increased 1.4%
•International Developmental Licensed Markets increased 4.2%
•Consolidated revenues increased 1% (1% in constant currencies).
•Systemwide sales increased 4% (4% in constant currencies).
•Consolidated operating income increased 7% (7% in constant currencies). Results reflected pre-tax charges of $56 million and $39 million for the current year and prior year, respectively, primarily related to restructuring charges associated with Accelerating the Organization. Excluding these current and prior year charges, consolidated operating income increased 8% (8% in constant currencies).**
•Diluted earnings per share was $3.51, an increase of 10% (11% in constant currencies). Excluding the current year charges described above of $0.06 per share, diluted earnings per share was $3.57, an increase of 11% (11% in constant currencies) when also excluding prior year charges.**
•The Company declared a 4% increase in its quarterly cash dividend to $1.93 per share.
*Refer to page 4 for a definition of Systemwide sales.
**Refer to pages 2 and 3 for additional details on our results for the third quarter 2026 and 2025.

Franchised restaurant margins are measured as revenues from franchised restaurants less franchised restaurant occupancy costs. Franchised restaurant occupancy costs include lease expense and depreciation, as the Company generally owns or secures a long-term lease on the land and building for the restaurant location.
Company-owned and operated restaurant margins are measured as sales from Company-owned and operated restaurants less costs for food & paper, payroll & employee benefits and occupancy & other operating expenses necessary to run an individual restaurant. Company-owned and operated margins exclude costs that are not allocated to individual restaurants, primarily payroll & employee benefit costs of non-restaurant support staff, which are included in Selling, general and administrative expenses.

MACROECONOMIC AND MARKET CONDITIONS
Unfavorable general economic conditions could adversely affect our business and financial results.
Our results of operations are substantially affected by economic conditions, including inflationary pressures, which can vary significantly by market and can impact consumer disposable income levels and spending habits. Economic conditions can be impacted by a variety of factors, including hostilities, epidemics, pandemics and actions taken by governments to manage national and international economic matters, whether through austerity, stimulus measures or trade measures, and initiatives intended to control wages, unemployment, credit availability, inflation, taxation and other economic drivers. Sustained adverse economic conditions or periodic adverse changes in economic conditions put pressure on our operating performance and business continuity disruption planning, and our business and financial results may suffer as a result.
Our results of operations are also affected by fluctuations in currency exchange rates, and unfavorable currency fluctuations could adversely affect reported earnings.
Health epidemics or pandemics could adversely affect our business and financial results.
Health epidemics or pandemics have in the past and may in the future impact macroeconomic conditions, consumer behavior, labor availability and supply chain management, as well as local operations in impacted markets, all of which can adversely affect our business, financial results and outlook.

These investments, developed in collaboration with franchisees, are designed to cater to consumer preferences, improve local business performance and increase the value of the McDonald's brand through the development of modernized, more attractive and higher revenue generating restaurants.
The Company requires franchisees to meet rigorous standards and generally does not work with passive investors. The business relationship with franchisees is designed to facilitate consistency and high quality at all McDonald’s restaurants. Conventional franchisees contribute to the Company's revenue, primarily through the payment of rent and royalties based upon a percent of sales, with specified minimum rent payments, along with initial fees paid upon the opening of a new restaurant or grant of a new franchise. The Company's heavily franchised business model is designed to generate stable and predictable revenue, which is largely a function of franchisee sales, and resulting cash flow streams.

Developmental License or Affiliate
Under a developmental license or affiliate arrangement, licensees are responsible for operating and managing their businesses, providing capital (including the real estate interest) and developing and opening new restaurants. The Company generally does not invest any restaurant capital under a developmental license or affiliate arrangement, and it receives a royalty based on a percent of sales, and generally receives initial fees upon the opening of a new restaurant or grant of a new license.

Our franchise business model presents a number of risks.
Our success as a heavily franchised business relies to a large degree on the financial success and cooperation of our franchisees, including our developmental licensees and affiliates. Our restaurant margins arise from two sources: fees from franchised restaurants (e.g., rent and royalties based on a percentage of sales) and, to a lesser degree, sales from Company-owned and operated restaurants. Our franchisees manage their businesses independently and therefore are responsible for the day-to-day operation of their restaurants. The revenues we realize from franchised restaurants are largely dependent on the ability of our franchisees to grow their sales. Business risks affecting our operations also affect our franchisees. If franchisee sales trends worsen, or if any of such business risks materialize or intensify, our financial results could be negatively affected, which may be material.
Our success also relies on the willingness and ability of our franchisees and affiliates to implement major initiatives, such as the restaurant modernization, operational, technological and training initiatives contemplated by our McDonald’s > NEXT strategy, which may include financial investment, and to remain aligned with us on operating, value/promotional and capital-intensive reinvestment plans.

The Company's revenues consist of sales by Company-owned and operated restaurants and fees from franchised restaurants operated by conventional franchisees, developmental licensees and affiliates. Fees vary by type of site, amount of Company investment, if any, and local business conditions. These fees, along with occupancy and operating rights, are stipulated in franchise/license agreements that generally have 20-year terms. The Company's Other revenues are comprised of fees paid by franchisees to recover a portion of costs incurred by the Company for various technology and digital platforms, and revenues from brand licensing arrangements to market and sell consumer packaged goods using the McDonald's brand.
Conventional Franchise
Under a conventional franchise arrangement, the Company generally owns or secures a long-term lease on the land and building for the restaurant location and the franchisee pays for equipment, signs, seating and décor. The Company believes that ownership of real estate, combined with the co-investment by franchisees, enables it to achieve restaurant performance levels that are among the highest in the industry.
Franchisees are responsible for reinvesting capital in their businesses over time. In addition, to accelerate implementation of certain initiatives, the Company may co-invest with franchisees to fund improvements to their restaurants or operating systems.
